I'm very sorry as I am the cause of delay when it comes to posting of all your submissions as I was away drinking my heart out. 

This page will be less and less active within the following days, weeks, months, and even years due to the reason that I will be focusing on myself. My physical, emotional, mental, and spiritual health.

For now, as we face the New Year, I would like to share with you my recent realization in life:

1. Life is not guaranteed. 
- Things come to our lives unexpectedly even how much we prepare ourselves. 

2. Love is not an emotion, it's a consistent choice.
- If you think you're in love with somebody right now, ask yourself: "Am I willing to choose this person everyday despite their flaws,  and imperfections? And knowing the fact that they might hurt me in some ways or another, will I be willing to forgive and forget those things just to make this thing work?"

3. No matter how clear and genuine your intention is, one can simply reject it.
- We cannot force people to choose us no matter how hard we try. If it's not you, then it's not you. 

4. Pour everything, until there's nothing left to give. 
- Run after them if you want to. Beg if you want to. But when you felt that it's been too much and you have nothing else to give, start walking away though it hurts. 

5. Love is just another part of our lives, there's more to life. 
- Trust me. It's not the end of the world if the two of you did not end up together. There's more to life. Trust the process and you'll see.

(rant and awareness)

There’s this bullying ass kissing culture on the department of nursing. It’s really sad how they tell us nursing is about compassion, solidarity, and patient advocacy. They tell us we are a team entering a profession where we must support each other.  But what they don't prepare you for is the cannibalistic, competitive, and utterly toxic culture that is relentless from the classrooms to duties.

There are classmates who live on a self-constructed pedestal of pretense, their halo polished so brightly it blinds the clinical instructor. They are the ones who nod vigorously at every theoretical concept, who submit their care plans looking like works of art, and who have mastered the art of the subtle, self-elevating comment aimed straight at your jugular.

I am talking about the PERFORMATIVE PERFECTS. And their favorite ammunition? YOUR MISTAKES.

We are students! We are here to learn. We are going to mess up the sterile field. We are going to calculate the IV drip rate wrong on the first try. We are going to forget a step in the 12-point check. These are human, forgivable errors in a controlled learning environment. Yet, for the Performative Perfects, my own group mates, my own classmates, no less these slip-ups are not learning moments; they are definitive proof of my inferiority. They watch, they catalog, and they bring it up with a smug, concerned look, often in front of others, just to reinforce their own fragile sense of superiority.

The absolute worst part is the hypocrisy. These are the same people who panic in private, who cheat on pre-tests, and who freeze up the second a patient deviates from the textbook script. Their entire perfection is a facade built on relentless ASS-KISSING toward the faculty and the strategic demolition of anyone who dares show vulnerability. 

This toxic bullying doesn't create better nurses; it creates terrified, isolated, and defensive ones. 

And if you’re one of those judgmental, "I'm perfect" classmates/batchmates/groupmates hear this: the real world doesn't care how well you recited the textbook and it also doesn’t revolve on how well your performance skills are. It cares if you can handle pressure, and it especially cares if you can treat your classmates/groupmates/batchmates the ones you’re tearing down now with the respect and decency you supposedly practice toward your patients.

Reply to #GreyhoundFreedomWall6271

I know it's hard to ve insecure and always feel anxious about what others think of us. But, we can't avoid wondering and judging looks that people will give us, nor make them adjust for our needs. 

They don't know you, and so do you. Which means that what you think they're thinking of about you, is just what you picture yourself to be in their pov. They probably don't even remember you after a few seconds or minutes because THEY DON'T KNOW YOU.

So often, we dig too deep into the pit of insecurities. But you know what? It's better to think that we are all just strangers to each other. That we know nothing about each other.

Those looks of judgement they are giving you? probably just observing your beauty.

Your blockmates/classmates smiling while looking at you? Probably they like you or knows someone who likes you. Maybe they like something about you (like the way you talk or your voice, the way you dress or present yourself, etc.) or they probably are just talking and coincidentally looked over your direction.

And if those people knew about what you think their opinions are about you, you might also hurt their feelings, or maybe make them feel offended.

Although your feelings are valid, it's also important for you to know that people don't care as much as you think they care about you (appearance-wise). So don't worry yourself too much and stop letting yourself down.

To all insecure people reading this, you are beautiful just the way you are. No matter how negative you think people say or think about you is just what you think of yourself—they are most likely admiring you, so worry not and rest assured, they think you're pretty and just can't openly express it! 

You don't have to rush and embrace the flaws that you think you have, take your time in accepting and start loving yourself more. I hope that you'll be gentler and kinder with your thoughts of yourself, because that's when real beauty will start blooming.

You’re still my best friend in my heart, but I know things have changed. I can feel you slowly becoming someone I used to know. And maybe that’s what hurts the most — watching you fade without completely disappearing. You’re still here, but not really.

I told you I was willing to change, but the truth is, I don’t know how. You were perfect in ways I’ll probably never be, and I kept expecting you to stay while giving you reasons to leave.

Maybe we’ve reached the part where love quietly becomes memory. You were the last person I thought I’d never lose. But I guess love changes things — sometimes for the better, sometimes for good.
And I’ll always carry that regret: that I wasn’t enough for the person who gave me every reason to be.

You kept trying to hold us together, but I was the one who kept letting go. You were ready to love me in all the right ways, and I was too lost, too unsure, to meet you halfway. I miss my best friend — the one who made me laugh at the dumbest things, the one who felt like home. I miss the comfort we had before feelings got in the way. I miss the version of us that didn’t have to think so hard just to talk, the one that didn’t hurt to remember.

To this guy… thank you for trying, for staying longer than you should have, for giving me parts of you I never deserved. Thank you for believing I could be better, even when I proved otherwise. You showed up for me in every way that mattered, and I’m sorry I couldn’t do the same.

I couldn’t change for you — not because I didn’t care, but because I didn’t know how. And that’s something I’ll always carry with me. You were the right person at the wrong time, and I hate that truth more than you’ll ever know.

So this is my quiet goodbye.
Not the kind that ends with anger or blame — just the kind that accepts what is. I’ll keep rooting for you from a distance, even if it hurts. I’ll keep wishing you peace, even if it costs me mine. Thank you for being my person, my safe place, my best friend.
You’ll always be one of the best parts of my life — even if I can’t be part of yours anymore. Now and forever :)

[rant]

Honestly, I still remember that one time back in elementary when I brought my guitar to school, and I wasn’t even allowed to go in. Ate guard took my name and section like I did something wrong, and when I tried to explain, she suddenly got mad and told me to get my guitar somewhere sa JHS office? I didn’t even know what to do because I was still an elementary student at that time. What annoyed me the most was that ate guard didn’t even bother to check my necktie — it was red, clearly showing that I was from elementary.

 Instead of shouting or getting mad, maybe she could’ve just double-checked before assuming. It’s frustrating when staff act like they already know everything but don’t even confirm the details first. Sometimes, a little patience and understanding go a long way. Don’t get mad at students if you haven’t even verified the situation properly.

yall might call me oa but the only reason I brought my guitar was for a performance task. I wasn’t trying to break any rule or show off or anything — I just needed it for school. But the way ate guard treated me made me feel like I did something wrong, when in reality, I was just doing what I was supposed to do. It honestly felt unfair and embarrassing, especially since I was still a kid back then.

I get that you’re doing your job, and I really respect that. But sometimes it feels like some guards forget that we’re students too. We’re not trying to cause trouble; sometimes, we just don’t know what to do. A calm explanation or a kind tone would’ve made such a big difference. It’s not that hard to be polite, and it actually helps more than getting mad right away.

That experience stuck with me because it was confusing and honestly a bit hurtful. I was younger, standing there trying to explain myself, but it felt like no one wanted to listen. So yeah, next time, ate guard, please be more observant and patient. Don’t let your mood decide how you treat people. If you’re unsure, double-check first. Don’t assume right away — because sometimes, the problem isn’t the student; it’s just a lack of understanding from the one in charge. 😛

share ko lang since bored ako this sembreak 😋
